body: Forward test of the management-tone-vs-delivery method (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell). Probability 0.45 (naive base rate 0.50) that: UltraTech Cement Q3 FY27 consolidated operating profit is ≥₹4,500 cr. Evidence: Q2 FY27 call (19-Oct-2026): volume +13.8% YoY, utilisation 71%, fuel and raw-material costs up (West Asia), other fixed cost/t −6%; Chairman's-office commentary: trade prices rose ₹7–10/bag in late September, 'Prices… have risen substantially in the month of October and continue to stay high. My sense is that there is more price improvement that will happen… in the next couple of months', 'full benefit… in the Q3 earnings'; South 'transforming. Mark my words.' Screener (₹ cr): OP Q3 FY26 3,911 (OPM 17.9%), Q4 FY26 5,599, Q1 FY27 5,015, Q2 FY27 3,719 (16.0%); sales Q2 FY27 23,295 (+19%). Reasoning: ₹4,500 cr needs roughly sales ~₹24.5k cr at ~18.4% OPM, i.e. the October price hikes must largely stick through the post-Diwali lull while fuel stays expensive. Management is unusually emphatic about prices; Indian cement hikes announced in October are often partly rolled back in November–December. We lean slightly below base. Resolution: YES if UltraTech's consolidated Operating Profit (screener.in quarterly table; equivalently EBITDA excluding other income from the results) for the quarter ended 31-Dec-2026 is ≥₹4,500 cr. Source: UltraTech Cement Q3 FY27 results (NSE) / screener.in consolidated quarterly table. Resolve by 2027-02-28; score with Brier vs base rate.

data.base_rate_reasoning: Naive: Q3 operating profit grows ~15% YoY in line with volume growth plus modest pricing, landing near ₹4,500 cr — a coin-flip-ish 50%.
